component.name: AppImage Manager
component.summary: Gestore di AppImage nativo per KDE

description.p: AppImage Manager integrates AppImages into KDE Plasma. When you click an AppImage in Dolphin, a confirmation dialog (kdialog) appears; on accept, the AppImage is copied into ~/.local/bin and a full KDE menu entry is created (icons + .desktop), then the application is launched.

AppImage Manager integra le AppImage in KDE Plasma. Quando fai click su un'AppImage in Dolphin appare una finestra di conferma (kdialog); se accetti, l'AppImage viene copiata in ~/.local/bin e viene creata la voce di menù di KDE (icone + .desktop), poi l'applicazione viene avviata.
Metadata is extracted directly from the AppImage squashfs payload via unsquashfs; the AppImage is never executed during install. Includes list and uninstall subcommands.

ul.li: Fixed the duplicate menu entry. Applications that register themselves on first run — Electron does this from app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient() — write ~/.local/share/applications/<name>.desktop pointing at the binary installed under ~/.local/bin. Because 0.1.2 stored our entry under a different desktop file ID (appimage-manager-<name>.desktop), the two coexisted and KDE showed the application twice. The entry is written under the canonical ID again, so a self-registering application replaces it instead of adding a second one, and any remaining duplicate pointing at a binary we manage is removed on install and list. Existing installs are migrated automatically.

list and uninstall now read a registry at ~/.local/share/app-image-manager/installed.list instead of scanning desktop entries for a marker, so an application that rewrites its own entry can no longer make an install invisible.

[Desktop Action …] groups are preserved (with their Exec rewritten to the installed binary). Dropping them while keeping the Actions= key that references them produced entries that violate the Desktop Entry specification.
Generated entries always carry Type=Application and never inherit a stale Hidden=true.

The icon cache is refreshed with xdg-icon-resource forceupdate, falling back to gtk-update-icon-cache --ignore-theme-index. The previous call failed silently because the per-user hicolor directory has no index.theme.

AppImage Manager no longer claims application/octet-stream. That MIME type is the generic fallback for any unrecognised binary file, so registering it as the default handler made the install prompt appear for files that are not AppImages. Only application/vnd.appimage and application/x-appimage are registered now, and upgrading (or re-running setup) removes the stale association.
The handle command now validates file contents: a file is only treated as an AppImage if it carries the type-2 magic, or is an ELF binary named *.AppImage. The extension alone is no longer enough.
MIME deregistration no longer deletes application/octet-stream associations belonging to other applications.

The installed .desktop entry is now saved with a namespaced filename (appimage-manager-<name>.desktop) instead of <name>.desktop. This avoids a collision with the .desktop entry an AppImage exposes from its own mount point, which caused KDE Plasma to hide the menu entry.

The installer now ensures KDE picks up the menu entry when ~/.local/share is missing from XDG_DATA_DIRS (it rebuilds ksycoca with the correct path and shows a user-facing hint with the permanent fix).
Click-to-install via kdialog with KDE menu integration.
Metadata extraction from the squashfs payload (no AppImage execution).
